articles.title: Home Assistant adds local drives to its storage settings
articles.dek: Internal and USB drives can hold backups, media and shared files through the same settings used for network storage.
body: Home Assistant adds a Local disk option to its storage settings, giving internal and USB drives a place alongside network shares. A device picker identifies the available partitions, and the owner chooses whether the storage holds backups, media or shared files.

Petar Petrov tested the interface against a live Supervisor with a USB flash drive. Write-protected devices stay read-only. Changing the read-only setting on a busy disk stops and asks the owner to close files or stop the apps using it before retrying.
The documentation names Supervisor 2026.10.1 as the required version and says no operating-system update is needed. The interface offers Local disk only when Supervisor supports it.

Document local disk storage
Unmount local disks eagerly and fail when the disk is busy

articles.title: Home Assistant follows an automation into the script it called
articles.dek: A direct link opens the exact child run instead of leaving you to match timestamps.
body: Home Assistant’s automation traces gain a direct link from a step to the script or automation run it started. Troubleshooting a chain of routines no longer requires finding the child run by its timestamp.

Jonathan adds the link to step details and the timeline, including individual repeat iterations and a script that calls itself. Browser back and forward preserve the selected run instead of returning to the newest one.
A step that starts several scripts still records only one child run. If the linked run has already left the stored history, Home Assistant explains that its trace is no longer available.

articles.title: Home Assistant shows gas use in the units on your bill
articles.dek: The Energy dashboard keeps therms and other shared energy units instead of always converting gas to kilowatt-hours.
body: Home Assistant’s Energy dashboard shows gas consumption in the unit used by its sources when they all agree. For households billed in therms, the gas chart and totals can use the same unit as the bill instead of always showing kilowatt-hours.

Colin Haven extends the rule to other energy units, including gigajoules and megawatt-hours, for both the current and comparison periods. Mixed-unit sources still use kilowatt-hours, as does a gas statistic also configured as an individual device; electricity is unchanged.
This is Haven’s first contribution to the frontend, reviewed by Petar Petrov. He checked the display with demo data and automated tests.

articles.title: Music Assistant cuts the wait when replaying a missed sentence
articles.dek: Short backward skips in podcasts and audiobooks reuse the audio already played.
body: Music Assistant makes short backward skips in streamed podcasts and audiobooks faster by retaining up to the last minute of played audio. Contributor OzGav reports that a ten-second rewind previously usually took about five seconds because the server had to fetch that audio again.

Quick repeated skips become one jump. The change uses the existing memory allocation; the smallest buffer setting retains less history. Skipping back more than a minute, or again immediately after a fresh fetch, still needs another request to the source.

articles.title: Device Database helps find products and compare prices
articles.dek: Search tolerates typos and recognizes categories, while device pages link to price-comparison sites by country.
body: The Open Home Foundation’s Device Database makes products easier to find and adds links to compare their prices. Searches tolerate misspellings and missing accents: “samsnug” finds Samsung, while “hue lighting” searches for Hue within the Lighting category.

Piero adds category recognition in the visitor’s language and highlights matching text. Device pages also gain links to price-comparison sites, with the country remembered from the previous choice or initially suggested from the browser’s timezone. These are links out to comparison services, rather than prices collected by the database.

articles.title: Home Assistant restores backups without unpacking an extra copy
articles.dek: Partial restores stop needing a temporary copy of the whole backup.
body: Home Assistant changes backup restoration so it can read the archive’s contents in place instead of first unpacking the entire outer archive beside the backup. That removes a temporary disk-space requirement even when restoring only one app or folder, and avoids writing and rereading the whole backup through a network share.

Stefan Agner applies the approach in Supervisor alongside Erik Montnemery’s work in Core. Supervisor also checks that a Home Assistant archive is present before stopping Core for its restore, so a missing archive fails earlier.

articles.title: Home Assistant switches heating when the waiting period ends
articles.dek: Generic thermostats stop leaving a heater on or off longer than the configured minimum cycle or cooldown.
body: Home Assistant corrects a timing error that could leave a generic thermostat’s heater running or idle past its configured waiting period. When a temperature reading arrived partway through a minimum cycle or cooldown, the next check waited the elapsed time plus the full period instead of just the time remaining.

Franck Nijhof makes the thermostat recheck at the actual deadline. In the reported failure, a heater stayed on until the next sensor reading half an hour later; regression tests cover a reading arriving midway through both kinds of waiting period.

pullRequests.title: Fix generic thermostat rechecking too late after a minimum cycle or cooldown

articles.title: ESPHome keeps ESP32 output pins steady through sleep
articles.dek: Makers can preserve an output’s electrical state through sleep and restart, with explicit restore settings.
body: ESPHome gives makers an option to keep an ESP32 output pin’s electrical state while the device sleeps or restarts. With the component configured to restore its state, an output can stay at the same level through deep sleep and waking instead of resetting.

Contributor luar123 adds the hold_state option and tests it on ESP32, ESP32-S3 and ESP32-H2. The output still needs its state set or restored after a reset. A pin configured for both input and output can briefly change level during waking, and removing a held pin from firmware through a wireless update does not release it until a hardware reset.

articles.title: Home Assistant’s installer checks a Proxmox server before sending credentials
articles.dek: Untrusted certificates require a deliberate trust decision and stay pinned for the setup session.
body: Home Assistant’s installer stops automatically accepting every Proxmox server certificate. Certificates trusted by the operating system follow the normal secure route; a self-signed, expired or mismatched certificate prompts the user before any credentials are sent.

The prompt explains the common self-signed setup and shows a fingerprint for comparison. Approval is tied to that exact certificate for the session: if it changes, setup stops and asks the user to reconnect and confirm the replacement. Retrying a password or entering an authentication code does not repeat the prompt for the same certificate.

pullRequests.title: Verify Proxmox TLS certificates before sending credentials

articles.title: Home Assistant gives screen readers clearer dialogs and form errors
articles.dek: Dialog titles become available to assistive technology, and empty required fields stop starting out as invalid.
body: Home Assistant corrects two accessibility gaps in common dialogs and inputs. Dialogs with ordinary titles, including confirmation, alert and prompt boxes, gain accessible names; required inputs stop announcing invalid data before the person has entered anything.

Franck Nijhof connects the inputs’ actual validation state to assistive technology. This is an initial correction: some dialogs with custom titles, including Assist and entity details, still need further work, and the contributor has not verified these changes with a screen reader.

pullRequests.title: Give dialogs an accessible name
Expose the real invalid state of inputs to screen readers

articles.title: Home Assistant selects Electrolux appliance programs
articles.dek: Compatible ovens and laundry and dishwashing appliances gain program choices, with additional appliance-specific settings.
body: Home Assistant adds program selection for compatible Electrolux ovens, washing machines, dryers, washer-dryers and dishwashers. Laundry appliances also gain temperature and spin-speed choices where supported.
The same addition exposes dehumidifier fan speed, hob and hood fan levels, and a hob’s sound and manual-or-automatic setting. The available choices follow each appliance’s capabilities.

pullRequests.title: Add select platform to Electrolux integration

articles.title: ESPHome controls Onkyo audio equipment through its wired remote port
articles.dek: The RI connection supports sending and receiving commands, tested with an A-9050 receiver.
body: ESPHome adds a wired control path for Onkyo receivers and other audio-video equipment using the RI remote-control connection. The new support sends commands and receives them, giving makers a way to connect compatible equipment through its wired port.
Steve Vigneau tested both directions with an Onkyo A-9050 and supplies the configuration guide. This is his first contribution to ESPHome, reviewed by J. Nick Koston.

pullRequests.title: [remote_base] Add Onkyo RI Wired Serial Support
[remote_base] Adds documentation for Onkyo RI wired serial protocol support.

articles.title: Music Assistant picks up podcast progress from more gPodder clients
articles.dek: Episode links count alongside identifiers, while newer listening positions remain in charge.
body: Music Assistant picks up listening progress from gPodder clients that identify an episode only by its web address. Those updates previously never reached Music Assistant, leaving people switching between podcast apps without the correct place to resume.

Fabian Munkes makes synchronization compare the time of each update so an older gPodder position does not replace a newer Music Assistant one. Opening an episode list stops adding another play for every listened episode. A full resynchronization can still add an extra play for entries already in the history.

pullRequests.title: Speed up the gPodder provider and fix its progress sync

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps keyboard users in place after menus
articles.dek: Closing a menu returns focus to its button instead of the top of the page.
body: Music Assistant returns keyboard focus to the button that opened a menu when someone presses Escape or chooses an option. Previously, menus on settings pages, player cards and media items could leave keyboard users back at the top of the page.
Marcel van der Veldt also handles submenus and leaves focus alone when the chosen action moves it into a dialog. Mouse and touch behavior stays the same.

pullRequests.title: Keep keyboard focus on the menu button after closing a menu
